summary.oneLiner: Vertically integrated cashew processor evolving into a diversified 'Food, Fuel, Feed and Fertility' agri-value platform under its long-term Strategy 2037 roadmap.
summary.business: Aelea Commodities Limited is a vertically integrated B2B and B2C agri-processing company that sources Raw Cashew Nuts from key African origins and Indian traders/MNCs and processes them into premium-quality cashew kernels and branded consumer products for domestic and international customers. Under Strategy 2037 the Company is progressing towards backward integration, by-product valorisation (CNSL, Cardanol, activated carbon, bio-charcoal) and renewable energy initiatives to build a circular, diversified agri-value enterprise.

currentContext.strengths: Vertically integrated B2B and B2C model spanning procurement, processing, grading, packaging, distribution, branding and value addition|Diversified raw-material sourcing: direct procurement from key African origins plus reputed Indian traders and MNCs, using pre-shipment, port-level and spot purchase models|Automation-led production and quality assurance systems at an FSSC 22000-certified manufacturing facility|Growing branded retail presence under 'Tryble & Supreme Cashew' across retail and e-commerce channels|Strategy 2037 diversification into cashew by-product valorisation (CNSL, Cardanol, activated carbon, bio-charcoal) creating additional revenue pools beyond kernel processing
currentContext.strategies: Strategy 2037: long-term roadmap to transform Aelea into an integrated 'Food, Fuel, Feed and Fertility' enterprise, diversifying beyond kernel processing into value-added food products, renewable energy, industrial applications, animal nutrition and sustainable agricultural inputs|Continued vertical integration across procurement, processing, grading, packaging, distribution, branding and value addition to improve control over quality, margins and customer experience|Growth via two new wholly-owned subsidiaries — Aelea Green Energy Limited (renewable energy, biofuel, sustainable solutions) and Aelea Nuts & Fruits Limited (value-added food processing, premium nuts, fruits, FMCG products)|Strengthening distribution and branded presence — organised retail, private label manufacturing, premium gifting, institutional ingredient supplies and global distribution channels|Evaluating downstream utilisation of cashew shells, husk and other by-products to strengthen the integrated value chain|Expansion guided by prudent capital allocation and financial discipline rather than pace of growth alone|Sustainability and circular-economy focus: maximising resource utilisation, minimising waste generation, and embracing circular economy principles
currentContext.expansion: Aelea scaled up its Surat Unit-II processing line during FY26, expanding installed capacity from 40 MTPD to 140 MTPD, with facilities spread across approximately 2,38,454 sq. ft. The Company has secured 2,38,454 sq. ft. of additional land for future expansion and, during FY26, completed land acquisition and laid the foundation for Unit III, which is planned to focus on Cardanol, Bio Charcoal and De-oil Cake production as part of its multi-phase backward-integration and by-product-valorization strategy (CNSL processing, Cardanol production, Activated Carbon, Bio-charcoal and other value-added applications). Under Phase I of its roadmap the Company intends to continue expanding processing capacity, improve operational efficiencies, strengthen procurement (local and global farm-gate sourcing) and increase automation. The Company also obtained additional term loans/working capital facilities during the year to fund this expansion.

risks.risk: Volatility in Raw Cashew Nut (RCN) prices
risks.note: RCN is the Company's core input, sourced from African origins and Indian traders/MNCs; price swings directly affect processing margins and working capital needs.
The business depends on cross-border shipment of RCN from African origins and export of finished kernels/products, exposing it to shipping and supply-chain bottlenecks.
Import of RCN and export sales, plus a foreign (UAE, AED-denominated) subsidiary, expose the Company to currency movements.
Flagged by management as a major risk in a global cashew processing industry with many established domestic and international processors.
Climatic uncertainty affecting RCN crop yields and availability is explicitly flagged as a risk to raw-material supply.
Export markets and institutional/branded customers require consistent compliance with food-safety and quality standards; a lapse could affect customer relationships and export readiness.
A commodity-processing, import/export-heavy model is working-capital intensive; management specifically flags working capital requirements as a major risk area.

risks.risk: Technology adoption and project execution risk on downstream integration
risks.note: Future by-product/renewable-energy projects (CNSL, Cardanol, Unit III, etc.) under Strategy 2037 carry execution and technology-adoption risk as the Company moves beyond core kernel processing.
